hints: Focus on the two big dips in transmittance, one around 2500 to 3300 and one around 1700, and think what functional groups absorb there.
The very broad absorption centred near 2900 $\text{cm}^{-1}$ is characteristic of an O-H bond in a particular functional group, not a simple alcohol.
Combine that broad O-H with the strong sharp C=O absorption near 1700 $\text{cm}^{-1}$ to identify which single molecule contains both groups.
walkthrough:
**Recall key IR absorptions**

Think like a detective. Different bonds absorb at different wavenumbers. The ones you need here are O-H and C=O.

$$\text{O-H (alcohol): } 3200-3600 \text{ cm}^{-1} \text{ sharp, } \text{O-H (carboxylic acid): } 2500-3300 \text{ cm}^{-1} \text{ very broad, } \text{C=O: } 1680-1750 \text{ cm}^{-1} \text{ strong sharp}$$

**Read the spectrum of X**

Look at the trace. There is a very broad, strong absorption with low transmittance from about 2500 to 3300 $\text{cm}^{-1}$ centred near 2900 $\text{cm}^{-1}$. There is also a very strong, sharp absorption near 1700 $\text{cm}^{-1}$.

So X must contain both that broad O-H type and a carbonyl group.

**Match to the four candidates**

Ethanoic acid is $\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$. It has $\text{C=O}$ and $\text{O-H}$ in a $\text{-COOH}$ group, so it shows both the broad 2500-3300 $\text{cm}^{-1}$ band and the 1700 $\text{cm}^{-1}$ band. That fits perfectly.

options.A: Ethanoic acid, $\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$, contains a carboxylic acid group. This gives a very broad O-H stretch from 2500 to 3300 $\text{cm}^{-1}$ due to hydrogen bonding, plus a strong C=O stretch near 1700 $\text{cm}^{-1}$. Both features are clearly present in the spectrum.
options.B: Ethanol, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$, has an alcohol O-H which absorbs as a narrower band at 3200 to 3600 $\text{cm}^{-1}$, not the very broad 2500 to 3300 band seen. It also has no C=O, so it cannot explain the strong absorption near 1700 $\text{cm}^{-1}$.
options.C: Ethylethanoate, $\text{CH}_3\text{COOCH}_2\text{CH}_3$, is an ester. It has a strong C=O near 1740 $\text{cm}^{-1}$ but has no O-H bond at all, so it cannot give the broad absorption around 2900 $\text{cm}^{-1}$. Students choosing this focus only on the carbonyl peak.
options.D: Propanone, $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3$, is a ketone. It has a strong C=O near 1715 $\text{cm}^{-1}$ but has no O-H bond, so it cannot give the broad absorption around 2900 $\text{cm}^{-1}$. Students choosing this also ignore the broad O-H region.
